source: Dış kaynaklarda saptanan eksik soru tipleri; bağımsız anlatım ve resmî cevap kontrolü (2026-10-13)
answer_convention: İki dilde aynı sırada; ilk şık doğru. Belirsiz cevap aktif bankada yok.
id_convention: Kalıcı idler_060.json; eski veya emekli kimlik yeniden kullanılmaz.

questions.text: For a navigation exercise, the planned leg is 110 NM and cruise groundspeed is 100 kt. Departure elevation is 1,000 ft AMSL and the planned cruise altitude is 5,500 ft AMSL. The planning instruction is to calculate the whole leg at cruise groundspeed, then add an extra 2 minutes for each 1,000 ft of altitude gained during climb. What is the estimated flight time, rounded to the nearest minute?
options: 75 minutes
66 minutes
77 minutes
57 minutes

questions.text: An aircraft is on the 123° magnetic radial of an identified, serviceable VOR, with a magnetic heading of 303°. Which OBS setting will centre the CDI and show a FROM indication?

A pilot compares three things after a windy flight: the route drawn before departure, the direction in which the nose pointed, and the path reconstructed from actual position fixes. Which navigation term applies to the third of these?
options: Track
Heading
Planned course
VOR radial

questions.text: For a basic GPS position solution, the receiver clock error is unknown but receiver height is supplied accurately from an independent source. With suitable geometry and no integrity-monitoring requirement in this exercise, what minimum satellite count can solve latitude, longitude and clock error?
options: Three
Four in every case, even with known height
Two
One

questions.text: A conventional Mode A squawk consists of four digits, each from 0 to 7. How many different four-digit codes are possible?
options: Only the three emergency codes

questions.text: What does attenuation of a radio-navigation signal mean?
options: A reduction in signal strength or power
A change in propagation direction at a boundary
Bending of waves around an obstacle
A mandatory increase in carrier frequency

questions.text: Where is the inclination (dip) of the geomagnetic field approximately zero, so dip-related magnetic-compass errors are least?
options: At the magnetic equator
At both geographic poles
At every point on the geographic equator, irrespective of the magnetic field
At the magnetic poles

questions.text: An aircraft flies a level arc at a constant slant range from a DME station. Why can a conventional DME-derived groundspeed read near zero although the aircraft is moving rapidly?
options: It measures change of range, which is near zero along the arc
It measures indicated airspeed and that must be zero
DME works only while parked
It directly measures wind speed, which must be zero

questions.text: Ignore Earth curvature. An aircraft is 3 NM vertically above a DME antenna and 4 NM horizontally from it. What uncorrected DME slant range should it indicate?
options: 5 NM
4 NM
3 NM
7 NM

questions.text: For reliable aircraft GPS reception, what is the main reason to give the antenna an unobstructed view of the sky?
options: Airframe masking can block required satellite signals
GPS must see the runway visually
It must receive a signal transmitted by the magnetic compass
A clear view eliminates all ionospheric and integrity errors

questions.text: A GPS displays geometric altitude and the pressure altimeter displays altitude with the applicable QNH setting. Which statement is correct for assigned barometric altitudes or flight levels?
options: GPS altitude can differ and does not replace the correctly set barometric altimeter
GPS geometric altitude is always identical to QNH altitude
The GPS altitude automatically becomes the assigned flight level
Any difference proves the pressure altimeter is faulty

questions.text: An exercise defines climb gradient as height gained divided by horizontal ground distance. Use 1 NM=6,000 ft. At 100 kt groundspeed and a 5% climb gradient, what rate of climb is required?
options: 500 ft/min
300 ft/min
5,000 ft/min
50 ft/min

questions.text: With other propagation conditions comparable, how does lowering frequency generally affect the useful range of a ground wave?
options: It generally increases the range
It always reduces the range to zero
It changes the wave into a GPS signal
It leaves the range independent of frequency

questions.text: On a normal Mercator chart, what generally happens to local scale as absolute latitude increases away from the equator?
options: It increases; distances must use the latitude scale appropriate to the area
It remains identical at every latitude
It decreases to zero toward the poles
Only longitude names change, with no scale effect

questions.text: What distinguishes Mode S surveillance addressing from the conventional four-digit Mode A squawk?
options: A unique ICAO aircraft address allows selective interrogation
The four squawk digits become decimal digits 0–9
Mode S never transmits aircraft identity
Mode S is a VOR bearing display

questions.text: In ADF navigation, what is quadrantal error primarily associated with?
options: Distortion of the received field by the aircraft’s characteristics
The geographic meridians converging
An incorrect QNH setting
Earth’s magnetic variation alone

questions.text: What is the pilot-relevant purpose of Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM) in a GPS receiver?
options: To assess solution integrity and warn when required integrity cannot be assured
To update the navigation database automatically
To guarantee zero position error in all conditions
To select QNH from the satellites

questions.text: Why is a sense antenna combined with the loop antenna in a conventional ADF?
options: To resolve the loop’s 180° directional ambiguity
To measure barometric altitude
To correct every coastal and night effect
To provide a DME distance reply

questions.text: A civil aircraft has normal VOR equipment and a compatible DME, but no TACAN airborne azimuth equipment. From a TACAN-only facility, which navigation information can it normally obtain?
options: DME distance, but not TACAN azimuth through its VOR receiver
Both TACAN bearing and distance through the VOR receiver alone
VOR bearing, but no distance
No distance because all TACAN signals are incompatible with civil DME

questions.text: A VOR being used for navigation transmits T-E-S-T instead of its normal identification during maintenance. What should the pilot do?
options: Do not rely on it for navigation; use another verified source and applicable notices
Continue because a centred CDI guarantees serviceability
Treat TEST as the normal station identifier
Increase the volume to make the bearing accurate

questions.text: A VDF bearing is explicitly reported as Class B. Under the accuracy classes in UK CAA CAP 413, what bearing accuracy is represented?
options: Within±5°
Within±2°
Within±10°
Exact, with no possible bearing error

questions.text: For a short-leg exercise, ignore convergence. A VOR radial is 090° relative to the station’s published magnetic reference, whose declination is 10°E. Local variation at the aircraft is 7°E. What TRUE bearing FROM the station corresponds to this radial?
A VOR can be received beyond its published protected service volume. What does reception alone establish there?
options: Only that a signal is being received; protected strength, quality and interference freedom are not assured
Full protected navigation coverage at every receivable distance
That terrain can no longer obstruct the signal
That the theoretical line-of-sight formula guarantees certified accuracy

questions.text: Use propagation speedc=300,000,000 m/s. What wavelength corresponds to a 100 MHz radio signal?
options: 3 m

questions.text: What does WGS 84 describe in GPS positioning, and why should a plotted chart’s coordinate datum be compatible?
options: A global geodetic reference; using a different chart datum can displace a correctly calculated position
The local QNH; it determines flight levels
A Mercator projection with constant scale everywhere
A guarantee that every database entry is current

questions.text: Which pair of points defines the Earth rotation axis, which is perpendicular to the equatorial plane?
options: The geographic North and South Poles
The magnetic North and South Poles
Greenwich and its antipodal point
The two intersections of the Equator and magnetic equator

questions.text: A conventional VOR CDI has 10° full-scale deflection to either side. Aircraft distance from the station is 60 NM (horizontal range; ignore height). The needle is one-fifth of full deflection. Using 1-in-60, approximately how far is the aircraft from the selected course?
options: 2 NM
1 NM
5 NM
10 NM

questions.text: Read point P on the fictional north-up graticule. Each small interval equals 6 arcminutes. What are its coordinates?
On a direct Mercator chart, which graduated margin should be used to convert a divider-measured route length into nautical miles?
options: The latitude scale near the route latitude
The longitude scale at any latitude
The latitude scale at the Equator regardless of route latitude
The compass-rose degree scale

questions.text: Which radio navigation aid is shown by the fictional chart symbol X?
options: VOR/DME
NDB without DME
VOR without DME
A civilian aerodrome beacon

questions.text: At the end of evening civil twilight, what is the position of the Sun centre relative to the unobstructed geometric horizon?
options: 6° below it
6° above it
12° below it
18° below it

questions.text: On a 16-point compass rose, north is 000° and each adjacent point is 22.5° apart. What direction in degrees is WNW?
What does a conformal aeronautical chart projection preserve locally?
options: Angles and shapes of sufficiently small areas
The area of every region without distortion
An identical distance scale everywhere
Every great circle as a straight line

questions.text: Ignoring time elapsed and local deviations of the date line, an aircraft crosses the International Date Line westward from 179°W to 179°E. What local calendar-date adjustment is required?
options: Add one day
Subtract one day
Add two days
No date adjustment because UTC also jumps by 24 hours

questions.text: For a normally paired VOR/DME installation with DME HOLD not selected, what happens when the pilot tunes the VOR frequency?
options: The equipment selects the associated paired DME UHF channel
DME measures only VOR signal strength
The pilot must always manually enter an unrelated DME frequency
The DME range is reset to zero regardless of position

questions.text: Which measured quantity is used by DME to calculate distance after accounting for the ground station fixed reply delay?
options: The elapsed time between airborne interrogation and received reply
The phase difference between two 30 Hz bearing signals
The strength of the VOR carrier alone
The difference between compass and magnetic heading

questions.text: For a fixed transmitted radio frequency, what Doppler changes occur when transmitter and receiver first approach each other and then move apart?
options: Received frequency is higher during approach and lower during recession
Lower during approach and higher during recession
It remains unchanged in both cases
Only signal amplitude changes; frequency cannot change

questions.text: What is the approximate propagation speed of radio electromagnetic waves in free space?
options: 300 km/s

questions.text: At the March and September equinoxes, what is the Sun approximate declination?
options: 0°; over the Equator
23.5°N at both equinoxes
23.5°S at both equinoxes
90°; over a geographic pole

questions.text: A GPS navigation display is configured to show cross-track error in nautical miles. What does a lateral CDI deflection represent?
options: A linear distance from the active selected track
An angular bearing error from the GPS satellite
Magnetic variation in degrees
Vertical distance above the waypoint

questions.text: An aviation GPS displays GS derived from satellite navigation without an air-data input. What speed is this?
options: Velocity over the ground
True airspeed relative to the air mass
Indicated airspeed from pitot pressure
Wind speed alone

questions.text: An aviation GPS moving-map database is expired. The pilot needs to check airspace and named waypoints for a VFR flight. What is the appropriate action?
options: Update using the approved database procedure and cross-check current charts; do not treat stale data as current
Change the GPS clock date to make the database appear current
Manually edit all published waypoint records to override the provider
Assume the satellite position fix automatically updates airspace and waypoint definitions

questions.text: Assume a spherical Earth where 1° of latitude is 60 NM. Two points lie on 60°N at 020°E and 030°E. What is the distance along that parallel (rhumb line)? Usecos 60°=0.5.
options: 300 NM
600 NM
150 NM

questions.text: Which list contains three physical carrier properties that can be varied to modulate a radio signal?
options: Amplitude, frequency and phase
Amplitude, frequency and propagation speed
Amplitude, wavelength and propagation speed
Frequency, phase and propagation speed

questions.text: In a constant crosswind, a pilot continuously turns to keep the fixed-card ADF needle straight ahead while approaching an NDB. What track normally results?
options: A curved homing track toward the beacon
The original straight desired track with automatic wind correction
A straight track away from the beacon
An orbit at constant distance from the beacon

questions.text: Compared with daytime, why can LF/MF NDB/ADF bearings be less reliable at night even when reception range increases?
options: Sky-wave or distant-station interference can disturb the bearing
VOR radials automatically replace all NDB bearings at night
The ADF needle changes from magnetic to true north at night
The NDB always stops transmitting when the Sun sets

questions.text: A pilot tracks inbound to an NDB on desired QDM 090°. Magnetic heading is 095°, and fixed-card ADF initially reads 355° (5° left). With heading held constant, the ADF later reads 358° and the beacon is stationary. What does the bearing geometry show?
options: QDM has become 093°; the aircraft is north/left of the desired 090° inbound line and needs a rightward intercept correction
QDM has become 087°; the aircraft is south/right of the desired line
QDM remains 090° because heading is unchanged
The ADF relative bearing alone proves that the NDB has moved

questions.text: In a fictional chart exercise, terrain elevation is 600 ft AMSL and a tower is 100 m high AGL. The planning instruction requires 1,000 ft above its top. Use 1 m=3.28 ft and ignore altimeter errors and other constraints. What minimum planned altitude is needed?
options: 1,928 ft AMSL
1,328 ft AMSL
1,600 ft AMSL
328 ft AMSL

questions.text: Which conventional reference meridian is assigned longitude 000°?
options: The Greenwich prime meridian
The magnetic meridian through magnetic north
The Equator
Every meridian through a geographic pole

questions.text: What distinguishes conventional primary surveillance radar from secondary surveillance radar (SSR)?
options: Primary uses an airframe-reflected echo; SSR uses a response to interrogation from a transponder
Primary always requires Mode C; SSR requires no onboard equipment
Primary measures only airspeed; SSR measures only wind
Both require the receiving pilot to transmit the callsign by voice for each sweep

questions.text: A conventional primary radar receives an aircraft echo. How is target range derived, and how is bearing derived?
options: Range from pulse round-trip time; bearing from antenna orientation
Range from antenna orientation; bearing from pulse round-trip time
Both from Mode C pressure altitude
Both from aircraft compass heading

questions.text: A pilot flies away from a VOR on the 270° radial using a conventional CDI, but leaves OBS set to 090° with TO showing. What is the effect of this reciprocal-course setup on lateral corrections?
options: Reverse sensing: steering toward the needle can move the aircraft farther from the intended outbound radial
The OBS changes automatically to 270°
The receiver changes the aircraft magnetic heading
The CDI is always centred whenever TO appears

questions.text: Under the conventional astronomical definition with a level unobstructed horizon, which part of the Sun disk defines sunrise and sunset?
options: The upper edge appearing at sunrise and disappearing at sunset
The centre crossing the horizon at both events
The lower edge crossing the horizon at both events
The centre reaching 6° below the horizon

questions.text: For this exercise, local standard time is UTC+3 h. A departure is planned for 01:20 local on 16 October. What UTC date and time should be entered?
options: 15 October,22:20 UTC
16 October,22:20 UTC
16 October,04:20 UTC
15 October,04:20 UTC

questions.text: Before using a tuned VOR for course guidance, what should the pilot positively verify?
options: The station actual transmitted identifier or correctly decoded identifier agrees with the intended charted station
The frequency alone is sufficient without identification
An expected name displayed from an outdated database is always sufficient
The CDI needle is centred, regardless of identifier

questions.text: While tracking inbound on an identified, serviceable VOR and then continuing through it on the same line, which indication most directly confirms station passage after the overhead ambiguity?
options: The TO/FROM indication changes from TO to FROM
DME necessarily reads exactly zero
The CDI must remain perfectly centred through the cone of ambiguity
The VOR identifier changes automatically

questions.text: In a conventional VOR receiver, which comparison provides the radial bearing information?
options: The phase difference between the reference and variable 30 Hz signals
The ground station reply delay to an interrogation pulse
The difference between aircraft IAS and TAS
The distance from the aircraft to four GPS satellites

questions.text: A serviceable VOR receiver has OBS 090°. The aircraft is east of the station, on radial 085° (five degrees north of the 090° radial). Ignore overhead ambiguity. Which conventional CDI indications are expected?
options: FROM, needle right of centre
TO, needle right of centre
FROM, needle left of centre
TO, needle centred

questions.text: A GPS receiver repeatedly loses satellite signals while a nearby VHF transmitter is keyed, then recovers after transmission stops. Which cause should be considered?
options: Radio-frequency interference, including possible transmitter harmonics
GPS needs VHF voice transmissions to calculate altitude
Selecting a distant waypoint consumes the satellite signals
All GPS signals stop worldwide whenever any aircraft transmits

questions.text: An aircraft stays at the same location with the same GPS satellite solution. The pilot only selects a more distant waypoint, without changing receiver mode or integrity requirements. Does that selection alone make the satellite-derived aircraft position less accurate?
options: No; fix accuracy is not determined by distance to the selected waypoint
Yes; position error necessarily doubles when waypoint distance doubles
Yes; a waypoint outside VOR range makes the GPS fix invalid
No; every GPS fix is perfectly accurate regardless of reception
